questions.q: Carlos Santos-Viola is most famous for being the primary architect for which religious organization, designing almost all of its major cathedrals and chapels?
o: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
questions.n: He designed the iconic Central Temple and established the 'look' for hundreds of INC chapels across the country.

questions.q: The 'Iglesia ni Cristo Central Temple' in Quezon City is Santos-Viola's most massive work. Which European style served as the primary inspiration for its pointed arches and soaring height?
questions.n: The use of pinnacles, spires, and pointed arches is a modern reinterpretation of the Gothic era's focus on 'reaching toward heaven.'

questions.q: Santos-Viola's designs are known for their 'Verticality.' Why is this important in his religious architecture?
o: To protect the building from floods
To draw the eye upward, symbolizing a spiritual connection to the heavens
To provide more space for cell phone towers
To save money on land by building upwards
questions.n: The repetition of vertical lines and spires creates a sense of awe and spiritual aspiration.

questions.q: Which of these is a signature feature of a Santos-Viola church facade?
o: Heavy, rusticated stone blocks with tiny windows
Tall, slender pinnacles and articulated spires
Rounded domes and clay tile roofs
questions.n: These elements give the buildings their distinctive 'reaching' appearance and identifiable silhouette.

questions.q: True or False: Carlos Santos-Viola graduated from the University of Santo Tomas (UST) and was a contemporary of fellow greats like Juan Nakpil.
questions.n: He was part of the pioneering generation of Filipino architects who helped define the country's post-war identity.

questions.q: Beyond the aesthetic, Santos-Viola was praised for the 'Functionalism' of his interiors. How did he improve the experience for worshippers?
o: Removing all seats to make more room
By adding movie screens to every wall
Building a shopping mall inside the nave
Designing column-free interiors and excellent acoustics for large congregations
questions.n: His buildings ensure that every member can see the pulpit and hear the sermon clearly without obstruction.

questions.q: The 'look' that Santos-Viola created for INC is so consistent that it is often called a 'Brand' of architecture. What benefit does this provide for the organization?
o: It prevents other religions from building churches
It creates a recognizable landmark that signifies the presence of the church in any community
It makes the buildings cheaper to paint
questions.n: The architectural silhouette serves as a powerful visual symbol of the church's identity and unity.

questions.q: Which of these materials did Santos-Viola frequently use to achieve the smooth, white, and crisp finishes of his chapels?
o: Reinforced concrete with plaster and paint
questions.n: This combination allowed for the complex geometric shapes of the spires while ensuring a clean, uniform finish.

questions.q: In his later years, Santos-Viola was honored for his contributions to the 'Filipino' identity. How does his work reflect a Filipino sensibility?
o: By making all his churches look like Spanish forts
By using only materials imported from the US
By adapting international styles (like Gothic) to the local climate and socio-religious needs of Filipinos
By building churches that look like Bahay Kubos
questions.n: He localized a Western style, making it a permanent and beloved part of the Philippine urban landscape.

questions.q: True or False: Carlos Santos-Viola is considered one of the 'Modernist' architects of the Philippines because he broke away from the traditional Spanish 'Antillan' church style.
questions.n: His work represents a major shift toward modern structural expression and away from the heavy, thick-walled colonial style.

questions.q: Carlos Santos-Viola was a devout member of which religion, despite designing the most iconic temples for the Iglesia ni Cristo?
questions.n: He remained a lifelong Catholic, demonstrating a professional ability to design for a different faith with deep respect and precision.

questions.q: What is the most recognizable color scheme used on the exterior of many churches designed by Santos-Viola?
o: White with Green or Blue trim
questions.n: This clean, bright palette helps the intricate vertical spires stand out against the Philippine sky.

questions.q: Which specific geometric shape is most dominant in the spires and pinnacles of Santos-Viola's church designs?
questions.n: The pointed, triangular peaks of his spires emphasize the upward 'reaching' motion of Neo-Gothic design.

questions.q: In Santos-Viola's designs, the 'spires' are often placed at the corners. What visual effect does this create for the building?
o: It frames the building and draws the eye upward to the sky
It makes the building look like a boat
It makes the building look shorter
questions.n: The placement of spires emphasizes the corners and creates a powerful, symmetrical silhouette.

questions.q: True or False: Most of Santos-Viola's chapels are designed with an open-air 'Bahay Kubo' style to save on electricity.
questions.n: His churches are typically enclosed, formal structures often designed for air-conditioning and high-quality acoustics.

questions.q: What kind of 'atmosphere' was Santos-Viola trying to create inside his large cathedrals?
o: A sense of order, solemnity, and awe
questions.n: The symmetry and vast, column-free spaces are designed to make the worshipper feel the grandeur of the faith.

questions.q: Which major Philippine university is Santos-Viola an alumnus of, along with many other National Artists?
questions.n: UST has a long history of producing the country's leading architects, including the masters of the 20th century.

questions.q: Why did Santos-Viola use 'pointed arches' instead of 'round arches' in his most famous churches?
o: To make the building look like a circle
Because they are easier to paint
To mimic the Neo-Gothic style which emphasizes verticality and 'reaching' for God
Because round arches were banned at the time
questions.n: Pointed arches allow for taller structures and reinforce the theme of spiritual aspiration.

questions.q: The 'brand' of architecture Santos-Viola created is so distinct that you can recognize an INC church even in other countries. What does this tell us about his design?
o: He successfully created a powerful visual identity that transcends geography
He only knew how to design one building
He used the same blueprints for every site without looking at the land
He wanted all buildings in the world to look the same
questions.n: His architecture functions as a 'visual signature' for the church, making it recognizable anywhere in the world.

questions.q: True or False: Carlos Santos-Viola's work is considered 'Ecclesiastical' architecture.
questions.n: This term refers specifically to the architecture of churches and religious buildings, which was his primary specialty.
